L1@P0: Tribute by H.E. President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf
L2@P0: In Memoriam: Dr. William Richard Tolbert, Jr.
L3@P0: Civil Servant, Politician, Farmer, Businessman & Minister of the Gospel
L4@P0: (May 13, 1913 - May 13, 2013)
L5@P0: Today, May 13, 2013, marks the 100th birth anniversary of Dr. William Richard Tolbert, Jr.,
L6@P0: Liberia’s 19th President, who served from July 23, 1971, to April 12, 1980.
L7@P0: President Tolbert was not merely a leader of the country, and a father to many Liberians, but also
L8@P0: a symbol of our national development during his lifetime. Trained as a civil servant, he was
L9@P0: attracted to politics and won in 1943, a seat in the House of Representatives on the ticket of the
L10@P0: True Whig Party, then the country’s only legal political party. He was later elected Vice
L11@P0: President to William V.S. Tubman, in 1955, and served in that position for 19 years until
L12@P0: President Tubman’s death in 1971.
L13@P0: Assuming the presidency, President Tolbert inherited a country with a single political party
L14@P0: controlled by a minority of the population; a modern economy almost totally in the hands of
L15@P0: foreign investors; and the majority of the indigenous population ostracized from both areas.
L16@P0: President Tolbert, conversely, shocked many and demonstrated enthusiasm not many had
L17@P0: expected, and which before long earned him the nickname “Speedy.”
L18@P0: Recognizing that Liberia was far behind and needed to catch up with the rest of the world, Dr.
L19@P0: Tolbert ushered in a new day with a resonating call for speedy development, self-reliance, selfsufficiency for the upliftment of the Liberian people, while ensuring integrity, patriotism,
L20@P0: diligence, dignity, and hard work.
L21@P0: In his foreign policy, President Tolbert adopted a more non-aligned posture, focused on
L22@P0: promoting Liberia’s political independence. He established diplomatic relations with the Soviet
L23@P0: Union, the People’s Republic of China, Cuba, and several Eastern Bloc countries. During the
L24@P0: Yom Kipper War, in October 1973, President Tolbert severed Liberia’s ties with Israel and
L25@P0: called for recognizing the national rights of the Palestinian people.
L26@P0: In the area of foreign relations, President Tolbert broke away from his predecessor’s pro-Western
L27@P0: doctrine. He also pointed out that the benefits of foreign investments were unevenly divided, and
L28@P0: he gradually re-negotiated concession agreements that had granted foreign investors important
L29@P0: tax and other privileges. He declared this concept “Humanistic Capitalism.”
L30@P0: A proponent of regional integration, President Tolbert was a signatory to the establishment of the
L31@P0: Mano River Union, the Economic Community of West African States and the African
L32@P0-1: Development Bank. He hosted the OAU Summit in Liberia and was elected its chairman.2
L33@P1: To improve the living conditions of the majority of the Liberian population, President Tolbert
L34@P1: advocated equity, justice and equal opportunity through such themes as: “Total Involvement for
L35@P1: Higher Heights,” “Rally Time,” and “From Mat to Mattress” – all aimed at creating “a
L36@P1: Wholesome Functioning Society” and success in the “War against Ignorance, Disease and
L37@P1: Poverty.”
L38@P1: During his tenure as Liberia’s 19th President, Dr. Tolbert opened the political space by allowing
L39@P1: the registration of opposition political parties in the country, lowering the voting age and
L40@P1: bringing more indigenous persons into government.
L41@P1: Through progressive policies, he expanded the educational and health systems; commence lowcost housing for the needy; established strategic specialized financial institutions in the
L42@P1: agricultural, housing and priority development sectors.
L43@P1: Since his death, 33 years ago, continuing efforts have been made to put the past behind us, to
L44@P1: reconcile and unite the Liberian people. In so doing, we memorialize his life and his contribution
L45@P1: to our country as politician, successful farmer and businessman, and a devout minister of the
L46@P1: gospel.
L47@P1: As we celebrate his 100th centenary under the theme: “Glorifying God, while celebrating the
L48@P1: legacy of Dr. William R. Tolbert, Jr.,” let us demonstrate all that he stood for - patriotism,
L49@P1: nationalism and respect for humanity. Let us pledge to live and work together to rebuild our
L50@P1: nation as he tried to do.
L51@P1: The Almighty God has brought us this far. May God continue to bless us and direct us as we
L52@P1: begin a new page in our nation’s history reflecting on the works and deeds of President William
L53@P1: Richard Tolbert, Jr. God bless Liberia!
